bull.argument: The filing shows a company with substantial financial resources and a growing set of revenue engines. Energy generation and storage revenue rose 27% to $12.77 billion, and gross margin in that segment expanded from 26.2% to 29.8%, with 46.7 GWh of storage deployed in 2025. Services and other revenue grew 19% to $12.53 billion. The company ended 2025 with $44.06 billion in cash and investments, up $7.50 billion, and operating cash flow of $14.75 billion nearly matched the prior year's $14.92 billion. Management states that 'Overall growth has allowed our business to generally fund itself.' Capital expenditures fell to $8.53 billion from $11.34 billion, even as the company builds AI, Robotaxi and factory capacity. Total gross margin held at 18.0% versus 17.9%. The bear case rests on falling automotive revenue and net income, which the filing does confirm, but the balance sheet and cash generation give the company room to invest through a difficult cycle.

claims.claim: Energy generation and storage segment grew strongly with improving margins
claims.quote: Gross margin for energy generation and storage increased from 26.2% to 29.8% in the year ended December 31, 2025

claims.claim: The company holds a large cash position and generates positive operating cash flow
claims.quote: We ended 2025 with $44.06 billion in cash and cash equivalents and investments, representing an increase of $7.50 billion from the end of 2024.

claims.claim: Management states that growth has allowed the business to generally fund itself
claims.quote: Overall growth has allowed our business to generally fund itself, and we will continue to make critical high-value investments while maintaining a strong balance sheet.

bear.argument: The filing's own numbers show a business under pressure at its core. Total revenues fell $2.86 billion to $94.83 billion, and net income attributable to common stockholders dropped $3.30 billion to $3.79 billion. Automotive sales fell 9%, and automotive gross margin slid from 18.4% to 17.8%. Your opponent leans on energy growth, but energy is a $12.77 billion segment, while automotive revenue of $69.53 billion still dominates and is contracting. Management concedes the business is exposed: it says trade policy 'could adversely impact consumer spending and demand for durable goods,' and that 'the removal of tax credits for electric vehicles' may affect demand. Meanwhile, the company expects capital expenditures 'in excess of $20 billion in 2026,' more than double 2025's $8.53 billion, and it carries $8.18 billion of debt. Operating cash flow of $14.75 billion is roughly flat, not growing, and it must now fund a much larger build-out. The filing also states the company 'may need or want to raise additional funds through the issuance of equity,' which would dilute shareholders. Investors are being asked to fund unproven bets, including Optimus, which the filing says has 'yet to commercialize,' at a time when the core business is shrinking.

claims.claim: Core revenue and profit declined in 2025
claims.quote: In 2025, we recognized total revenues of $94.83 billion, representing a decrease of $2.86 billion compared to the prior year.

claims.claim: Planned 2026 capital spending sharply exceeds 2025 levels, raising funding needs
claims.quote: We currently expect our capital expenditures to be in excess of $20 billion in 2026

claims.claim: Company may need to issue equity, risking dilution, and the Bots business is unproven
claims.quote: We have yet to commercialize Bots and cannot predict how demand for Bots will develop

bull.argument: The bear case is right that core automotive revenue fell 10% to $69.53 billion and net income dropped to $3.79 billion, and I do not dismiss that. But the filing's own framing points to resilience. Total gross margin held at 18.0% versus 17.9%, because energy gross margin rose to 29.8% and services and other revenue grew 19% to $12.53 billion. Energy is a $12.77 billion segment growing 27%, which is no longer a side bet. On the 2026 spend, the filing says capex is expected 'in excess of $20 billion' but also that 'we believe this strategy will position our Company for further growth as we make investments in a capital efficient manner.' Management also notes it can 'adjust our capital and operating expenditures by operating segment' if ramps slow, which limits downside. Liquidity is substantial: $44.06 billion in cash and investments, plus $6.43 billion of unused committed credit against $8.18 billion of debt. Management says it expects 'to continue to generate net positive operating cash flow.' Equity issuance is a possibility the filing mentions, not a plan it commits to.

claims.claim: Energy segment is growing with expanding margins and now provides a meaningful offset to automotive weakness
claims.quote: Energy generation and storage segment revenue increased $2.69 billion, or 27%

claims.claim: Management can scale capital spending down if ramps slow, limiting downside from the 2026 build-out
claims.quote: we expect that if needed we will be able to adjust our capital and operating expenditures by operating segment

claims.claim: Management expects continued positive operating cash flow and has substantial liquidity
claims.quote: We generally expect to continue to generate net positive operating cash flow.

bear.argument: Your opponent's segment math is accurate, but it doesn't rebut the core problem. Total gross margin held at 18.0% only because energy and services offset weakness in cars. The filing says gross margin for total automotive 'decreased from 18.4% to 17.8%,' and automotive revenue, which is still $69.53 billion, fell 10%. Energy growth is real, but it is a $12.77 billion segment supporting a business whose largest engine is shrinking. On funding, the filing states that 'we currently expect our capital expenditures to be in excess of $20 billion in 2026,' against $14.75 billion of operating cash flow. The 'adjust' language is a conditional option, not a funding source. The filing is explicit that heightened capex 'will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow.' Cash of $44.06 billion looks large, but it is being drawn down: capex and investing outflows of $15.48 billion exceeded operating cash flow in 2025, and debt stands at $8.18 billion. The filing also says the company 'may need or want to raise additional funds through the issuance of equity.' Even if that is not yet a plan, it is a real dilution risk for shareholders funding unproven programs such as Bots, which the filing says it has 'yet to commercialize.'

claims.claim: Automotive gross margin declined, so total margin stability is propped up by other segments
claims.quote: Gross margin for total automotive decreased from 18.4% to 17.8%

claims.claim: 2026 capital spending is expected to exceed operating cash flow, requiring outside funding
claims.quote: will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow

claims.claim: Planned 2026 capex is more than double 2025 levels
claims.quote: We currently expect our capital expenditures to be in excess of $20 billion in 2026

judge.reasoning: The bear's cited quotes all verified, including the explicit statement that heightened capex 'will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow,' which directly undercuts the bull's self-funding thesis. The bull's energy-growth quote was unverified, and its 'adjust capex' and 'net positive operating cash flow' points do not address the stated 2026 funding gap. The bear answered the bull's margin-stability argument by showing automotive margin decline was masking underlying weakness, while the bull's responses were less direct on the funding question.
